readings.claim: New Mexico's labour markets are not its counties. In the only part of the state where the data exists to check, one county imports at least 9,390 workers while its neighbours send 45% of theirs out.
basis: QWI 2024-Q4 ownercode A05, private employers, nine counties
ACS B08007 2020-2024, place of work, same nine counties
readings.support: Los Alamos County holds 19,551 private jobs against 10,161 resident workers who work in-county, a gap of 9,390. Rio Arriba sends 44.8% of its resident workers out of the county, Sandoval 47.4%, Mora 44.6%.
readings.qualifications: QWI counts private employers only, so government jobs are excluded and adding them could only raise the workplace count: 9,390 is a floor, not an estimate. The negative gaps for the other counties are uninterpretable for the same reason — a negative gap is what a missing public sector looks like, and Santa Fe is the state capital. The two sources are different universes over different periods, a quarter against five years.
readings.rivals: The gap could be filled by multiple job-holding rather than in-commuting, or by workers living in Los Alamos County who are missed by the ACS place-of-work universe.
readings.geography: nine of 33 New Mexico counties — the only ones with employer data

readings.claim: The largest single flow of outside money into a New Mexico county cannot be traced to anyone. $5.28bn was spent performing federal work in Los Alamos County in FY2025; $75M went to recipients registered there; and neither number says where the value ended up.

readings.qualifications: Recipient location is the registered address, often an out-of-state headquarters; place of performance differs sharply (e.g. Los Alamos FY2025: $75M by recipient vs $5.28B by place). readings.claim: New Mexico's most consequential internal dependency — extraction revenue in the southeast paying for services everywhere else — breaks at its last step, because no allocation of state spending to places exists.
readings.support: New Mexico oil production passed 2 million barrels a day in 2024, more than double 2019, and oil and gas proceeds fund an increasing share of state government. A federal royalty rate cut from 16.67 to 12.5 per cent reduces state revenue at unchanged production.
readings.qualifications: The $1.7bn figure is an external estimate cited in reporting, not an observation. State revenue overall is reported still rising, with forecasters describing roughly $1bn more for the next budget, reported alongside the observation that the state budget is booming and the economy is not — two different things. Whether the state spends, saves into permanent funds, or both is UNKNOWN. State spending as a share of household income is UNKNOWN because FED_SPEND_SHARE_NNM is unobserved and WR062 says state figures cannot be apportioned to eight counties without an allocation rule the model does not have. The federal_fiscal machine holds federal flows, not state ones, so this chain is not modelled. What would change the view is an allocation of state spending to counties, which does not exist. Two counter-mechanisms are held against this: production growth offsets the rate cut, and investment income substitutes for extraction revenue, as reporting describes.
readings.contradictions: Production growth offsets the rate cut. Investment income substitutes for extraction revenue, as reporting describes.
readings.rivals: The rule only bites on federal acreage, so federal versus state land production shares would discriminate how much of the state's revenue is exposed to it at all.

readings.claim: Federal money reaching New Mexico cannot have one statewide effect. In Los Alamos County it arrives as the entire private economy; in Mora County, 60 miles away, it arrives only through whatever the 44.6% who already commute out can reach.
readings.support: Los Alamos County: 19,551 private jobs in a county of about 19,000 people, average private earnings $11,370 a month, and 3.0% of residents working outside the county. Mora County: 394 private jobs, average private earnings $3,984, 44.6% of resident workers working outside the county and 10.8% travelling 60 minutes or more.

readings.rivals: The difference may be scale alone rather than structure — Mora is small enough that any concentrated employer would dominate it the same way.

difference.conclusion: The same federal force reaches these two counties through different structures and therefore cannot have the same local effect. In Los Alamos it arrives as the county's entire private economy, concentrated in one place of performance. In Mora, 60 miles away, it arrives — if at all — through whatever the 44.6% who already leave the county are able to reach. One county's exposure is its employment; the other's is its commute.
difference.unknown: Whether any of Mora's out-commuters reach federally funded work at all. No published flow connects a worker's county of residence to a county of employment in this state, so the second half of this comparison is a structural difference, not a measured one.

chain.name: A labour market in one county becomes housing pressure in the counties around it

links.mechanism: Jobs located in Los Alamos County exceed the county's resident workers working in-county by at least 9,390, and the county's own housing stock cannot house them: 62.1% of it predates 1980 and its capacity to add units is unobserved.
links.flow: FL_LABOR_INTO_LOSALAMOS — a labour flow into the county, observed as a lower bound from two independent federal sources
links.intermediate: households who hold a Los Alamos County job and a house somewhere else, and the housing markets of the counties they live in
links.receiving_place: the surrounding counties — Rio Arriba, Santa Fe, Taos — where 7,075, 10,128 and 1,658 resident workers respectively work outside their county
links.parameter: housing cost relative to local earnings in the receiving counties: a household earning $11,370 a month bids for housing in a county whose own average private earnings are $4,885 (Rio Arriba) or $4,179 (Taos)
links.counter_mechanism: The commuters may be dispersed widely enough that no single receiving market feels them; or the housing in question may be the seasonal and other-vacant stock already counted (HC01: 13,607 seasonal and 11,277 other vacant units in the region), in which case the pressure is on a different margin than new construction.
links.falsifier: A published county-to-county commuting matrix showing that Los Alamos County's in-commuters come overwhelmingly from inside Los Alamos County's own housing market or from outside the state would break this chain at its first link.

counterfactual.constraint: BN_LABORSHED_HOUSING — housing within reach of the Los Alamos labour market
counterfactual.if_reduced: If housing within commuting range of those workplaces were materially easier to obtain
actors_change: Households holding Los Alamos County jobs choose location on wage and amenity rather than on what is available within a tolerable drive.
Employers at those workplaces recruit from a wider pool, because the binding question stops being where a hire could live.
Builders in Santa Fe and Sandoval — where construction employment is concentrated (HC08) — face demand in counties they are not observed to work in, and whether they would is unobserved (HF04, HF11).
parameters_move: commute time in the receiving counties, which is observed and would fall
housing cost relative to local earnings in Rio Arriba and Taos, where a $11,370 household currently bids against a $4,885 or $4,179 local average
the effective wage net of travel for the in-commuting households
becomes_possible: Local earnings and local housing cost in the receiving counties stop being set by a labour market those counties do not contain.
counterfactual.next_constraint: Serviced land and construction capability. RC02 records that a community water system existing is not service capacity and that connection capacity is unobserved; RC01 records crew and project throughput unobserved. Relieving housing demand would move the constraint onto two capabilities the model cannot measure.
could_offset: The 13,607 seasonal and 11,277 other-vacant units already in the region (HC01) could absorb the demand without any construction, in which case the constraint was never production.
New housing near the jobs could draw households out of the receiving counties rather than adding to them, moving the problem rather than easing it.
counterfactual.not_a_forecast: No magnitude is claimed. Every step is a mechanism the model already holds, not a simulated quantity.

The retention decomposition refuses D3 to D5 in terms: reading a registration address as where value went is the error that makes a Delaware entity look like a Delaware economy.

leakage.what_leaves: wages earned at Los Alamos County workplaces by people who live in other counties

Calling it leakage from Los Alamos County would make a working labour shed look like a loss, and would miss that the receiving counties are the beneficiaries.

overrepresented.geographies: The eight northern counties plus Bernalillo carry every labour, firm and earnings observation in this repository. They are nine of 33 counties and about half the state's population, and they are where almost all of this reading's specificity comes from.
overrepresented.systems: Housing and food are modelled in depth; energy, health, education, manufacturing and the visitor economy are present as world conditions or not at all.

refusals: No county estimate is manufactured from a statewide value.
No missing geography is interpolated and published as observed.
No edge rests on two places being adjacent.
No outflow is called a loss without evidence it could have compounded here.
No stock is read as a capability.
Tribal and Pueblo geographies are not modelled as county subdivisions, and the absence of public data about them is not read as economic absence.
No single number for the state is computed, and no place score exists.
